description.narrative: 4.2 Proportion of land with dongas in programme area, degraded land rehabilitated with support from this Action.

comment.narrative: In general the indicator is implausible as target values are unpredictable due to unknown expansion rates of the gullies during the Action. Based on 2019 gully size values 468 hectares of gullies would need to be rehabilitated which equates to costs of at least 7.5 Mio. EUR. Furthermore at a certain size threshold it becomes uneconomical to rehabilitate gullies. The approach of ReNOKA and the Action is therefore to halt further erosion head cutting through a combination of measures such as improved rangeland management stormwater diversion and detention terrace rehabilitation clearing of invasive plants head stabilisation checkdams and revegetation.

comment.narrative: Construction of combinations baskets of emergency rehabilitation measures at 4 hotspots in 2 priority subcatchments is nearing completion early 2023 to stabilise and restore 160 hectares of watersheds. Rapid rangeland rehabilitation measures e.g. removal of invasive shrubs construction of stones lines and gully erosion control measures by CWTs and their members has led to the rehabilitation of a further 116 hectares in 8 watersheds. The reported areas of rehablitated watersheds include previously degraded rangelands gulley erosion and degraded wetland areas. Reporting is aligned with proposed revisions to the Output 4 Logframe indicators Areas of watersheds rehabilitated with baskets of measures. rather than the current logical framework.The ROM report recommended that the indicators especially of output 4 need to be further developed to measure the success of the activities at the community level including behavioural and physical outcomes that can realistically be achieved within the scope and time frame of the Action. The Midterm Review MTR will further look into an indicator and log frame revision.
